description: Sends up to 100 emails in one call, each with its own agent, recipients and content. A message that fails is reported in its place in `data` and does not stop the others. Sent mail cannot be recalled.

idempotency_key.description: Any string up to 255 characters: a call repeated with the same key returns the first answer instead of acting twice. Without it, the call gets a key of its own.

messages.description: The emails to send, each with its own agent, recipients, subject and body.

agent.description: Which agent sends this message: its name or `agt_` id. Optional, as on `POST /v1/messages`: leave it out and `from` names the agent, or the workspace's single agent sends. A key tied to one agent always sends as that agent and may leave this out. Required only when the workspace has several agents and `from` names none of them; without it, that message fails with `missing_field`. In a workspace with no active or paused agent, the first one is created when the key may create agents (the `manage` scope); otherwise that message fails with `insufficient_scope`. An unknown agent fails only that message, with `agent_not_found` (`agent_archived` for an archived one), and a key tied to one agent fails it with `insufficient_scope` for any other, named here or in `from`.

bcc.description: Addresses to blind-copy, up to 50. They receive the message but appear in none of its headers.

body_html.description: HTML body, up to 1,000,000 characters. With `body_text` as well, the email carries a plain-text part and an HTML part.

body_text.description: Plain-text body, up to 1,000,000 characters. At least one of `body_text` and `body_html` is required, or their aliases `text` and `html`.

cc.description: Addresses to copy, up to 50. Every recipient sees them.

from.description: The sender you want, as on `POST /v1/messages`. Without `agent`, `billing`, `billing@acme.com` and `Acme <billing@acme.com>` all mean the agent called `billing`, and never a different agent. If there is none, it is created when the key may create agents (the `manage` scope) and your plan has room; otherwise only that message fails, with `insufficient_scope` or `plan_limit_exceeded`. Beside `agent`, only its display name is used: `agent` decides the sender. Either way a display name in it goes on the From line, a scheduled item's too. The address that sent comes back as `from` on the message's result.

html.description: Alias of `body_html`: used when `body_html` is left out, ignored when both are sent.

in_reply_to_message_id.description: Id of the message this one answers (`msg_…` or `rcv_…`), named in the email's `In-Reply-To` header. The message joins its thread when the same agent sent or received it. Left out, it starts a new thread.

list_unsubscribe.description: Opt in to RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe: the message carries `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` headers, so the recipient's mail app shows an Unsubscribe button. One click suppresses the address for your whole workspace: every later send to it from any of your agents is refused with `recipient_suppressed` until you allowlist it (`POST /v1/suppression/allow`). Turn it on for newsletters, digests and other recurring mail. Leave it off (the default) for password resets, sign-in links, receipts and anything else the recipient must keep receiving. Needs exactly one `to` recipient and no `cc` or `bcc`.

metadata.description: Your own key-value strings, kept with the message and returned by `GET /v1/messages/{id}`; they are not part of the email. Keys up to 64 characters, values up to 500.

references.description: Message-IDs for the `References` header. Write one from another system with its angle brackets (`<…>`); a value without them is read as a mails.ai message id.

reply_to.description: The address replies should go to. Left out, replies go to the agent's `receiving_address`.

scheduled_at.description: Send this message at this time instead of now: an ISO 8601 UTC time ending in `Z`. A time in the past sends at once.

tags.description: Up to 10 name-value labels, kept with the message and included in its `message.sent` event; they are not part of the email.

name.description: Tag name: 1 to 256 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

value.description: Tag value, up to 256 characters; it may be empty.

text.description: Alias of `body_text`: used when `body_text` is left out, ignored when both are sent.

to.description: Who the message goes to: one address, or a list of 1 to 50.

name: mails_emails_send_batch
title: Send a batch of emails
